x-bump-note: 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0: two review findings. (1) Added an anchored filename-safe `pattern` to `target_id`, mirroring priority-intent.schema.json's — defence in depth, since this schema's own description says target_id IS the filename, and relying solely on a different schema's upstream validation is a single point of failure. (2) Added an allOf if/then enforcing `source_repo` is null exactly when `source` is `op` (previously prose-only in `source_repo`'s description; a claude-klabauter-side docstring wrongly claimed the schema already enforced it). Classified MAJOR because both changes reject instances that previously validated (a target_id shape the new pattern excludes; a source/source_repo combination the new if/then excludes).
description: Priority-ledger entry — an authored priority assignment for one target, one file per target under state/priority-ledger/<target-id>.yaml. NEGATIVE-SPEC (1): there is NO `id` field — target_id IS the filename (one file per target, <target-id>.yaml), per the filename-as-identity invariant (D2, coordinator/docs/wiki/canonical-artifact-shapes.md:1035-1049). NEGATIVE-SPEC (2): NO `inherited_from` / `resolved_from` / `priority_predecessor` field is permitted on this schema — resolved-from provenance is derived-emission-layer only, never authored data; an entry recording how a priority was walked/inherited belongs to a downstream emission artifact, not this ledger. `priority: none` is the EXPLICIT-CLEAR SENTINEL: a real authored assignment that terminates an upward inheritance walk, NOT a deletion — do not conflate an absent file with a `none`-priority file. additionalProperties: false — this schema is closed by design (unlike the permissive bug/debt-backlog schemas), because the derived-emission-layer boundary above is a security/correctness boundary, not a forward-compatibility nicety.

target_id.description: Identifier of the prioritized target. Matches the filename (<target_id>.yaml) — see NEGATIVE-SPEC (1) in the top-level description; there is no separate `id` field. Pattern mirrors priority-intent.schema.json's target_id pattern (defence in depth, review finding): rejects path-traversal shapes ('..', '/', '\\', leading '.') and a trailing '.' (Windows silently strips a trailing dot, which would alias two distinct-looking target_ids to the same on-disk file) — only safe filename-component characters are accepted.

target_kind.description: The kind of artifact target_id refers to.

priority.description: Priority tier, ordered urgent (hottest) > high > medium > low > none. `none` is the EXPLICIT-CLEAR SENTINEL — a real authored assignment that terminates an upward inheritance walk, NOT a deletion.

set_by.description: Identifier of the session/agent/person that set this priority.

source.description: The writing MECHANISM that produced this entry — never a consumer repo name (do NOT write e.g. "cockpit-intent" here; use source_repo for that).

source_repo.description: The originating repo identifier for this entry; null when source: op. Enforced structurally (not just by this prose) via the schema's allOf if/then: source: op requires source_repo null (when present), source: external-intent forbids an explicit null (review finding — a claude-klabauter-side docstring previously claimed this was already enforced when it was not).
